Balanced but more cautious. The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 2.25–2.50%, citing a strong labor market and moderate growth, but with inflation below 2% and soft business fixed investment; market-based inflation compensation declined while longer-term survey expectations were little changed. Uncertainties increased, prompting a risk‑management stance; Bullard dissented in favor of a 25 bp insurance cut.

Beige Book context (covering April to mid-May across Districts) aligns with this mix: activity was modest, labor markets remained tight with shortages of low-skill workers and wage pressures in select occupations, and consumer spending/vehicle sales were steady to modest. Manufacturing, residential construction, and real estate contributed, tourism was stronger in the Southeast, but agricultural conditions remained weak. Importantly, the April 2019 SLOOS showed banks tightening standards and terms for C&I and construction/land development loans, with weaker loan demand across construction/land development and several consumer categories (HELOCs, credit cards, other consumer), and roughly unchanged demand for autos and subprime mortgages. These tighter credit conditions and softer loan demand are consistent with softer capex and could restrain consumer credit, reinforcing the FOMC’s cautious tone.

Net tone: mildly positive on current conditions but more cautious on the outlook via the credit channel. Adjusting for the Beige Book/SLOOS, the overall stance edges closer to neutral from the prior mildly positive read.
